_comment: The criterion-readability ratchet for PRODUCT_SPEC.md (SPEC INV-287, INV-288). Four arms, one per reading defect the 2026-07-27 body survey measured: a criterion that welds the whole rule into one sentence, a criterion that defines its own term in place while the glossary already owns that fact, a criterion whose closing clause has no finite verb, and a criterion whose anchor competes with its prose. Each arm carries its own threshold and its own recorded baseline: the count of criteria that break it today. A count above the baseline reds. A count below it is a fall, and `--rebaseline` writes the lower numbers back; no run raises a baseline, and a raise is a deliberate edit here with its reason stated, run through the pipeline (INV-288).

long-criterion.reds: a criterion whose sentence runs past the word cap
long-criterion.fix: state the trigger and the duty and stop; move an enumeration into a sub-list, and a `since` or `so that` clause into its own short sentence or a note.

inline-gloss.reds: a criterion that defines a term in place, in a dash-pair aside or a parenthetical
inline-gloss.fix: give the term one glossary entry and let the criterion use it; a term not worth a glossary entry is not worth a gloss.

absolute-tail.reds: a criterion closing on a noun phrase with no finite verb
absolute-tail.fix: make the closing clause a finite sentence with its own subject and verb, or cut it.

anchor-noise.reds: a criterion whose anchor carries too many codes, or that runs a code anchor or code spans through its prose
anchor-noise.fix: an anchor needing four codes marks a criterion carrying four rules — split it; keep every code anchor at the line's end and cut the code spans the sentence can name in words.

reason: Baselines seeded at the row-148 readability landing, measured over the live PRODUCT_SPEC.md as the working tree stood on 2026-07-27 (1461 criteria): long-criterion 469, inline-gloss 120, absolute-tail 147, anchor-noise 61. The committed HEAD of that day measured 60 on anchor-noise over 1452 criteria, so the seed carries one unit from a delivery still in flight; the first run after the tree settles reports the fall and `--rebaseline` records it. Every later delivery lowers these or leaves them (INV-288).
